prompt: Read the English sentence: 'Not all students failed the exam.' Does this mean: (a) At least one student passed, (b) All students passed, or (c) No student passed? Respond with only the letter, no explanation.
notes: Tests external negation of universal quantifier.
alternate_prompt: What follows from this sentence: 'Not all students failed the exam.' Does this mean: (a) At least one student passed, (b) All students passed, or (c) No student passed? Reply with the letter alone.

prompt: Read the English sentence: 'None of the students failed the exam.' Does this mean: (a) At least one student passed, (b) All students passed, or (c) No student passed? Respond with only the letter, no explanation.
notes: Minimal pair for en-neg-001a: negates an existential ('none of') rather than a universal ('not all'), so the correct reading flips from 'at least one passed' to 'all passed'. Isolates whether the model distinguishes ¬∃ from ¬∀ rather than pattern-matching negation+quantifier surface forms to a single default reading.
alternate_prompt: What follows from this sentence: 'None of the students failed the exam.' Does this mean: (a) At least one student passed, (b) All students passed, or (c) No student passed? Reply with the letter alone.
